title: Gothenburg and Chalmers Researchers Develop Modular Graph Neural Decoder for Surface Code Memory and Lattice Surgery - Quantum Computing Report
gist: University of Gothenburg and Chalmers researchers built a renormalization-inspired modular GNN+GRU neural decoder for surface codes that stays at ~2-3M parameters across distances 3-9, trains on one GPU, beats MWPM on IBM Nighthawk r1 data, nearly matches AlphaQubit on Google Sycamore data and decodes a real lattice-surgery ZZ-merge. Real-time deployment still requires sub-microsecond inference on FPGA/ASIC.

insights.claim: Gothenburg and Chalmers researchers designed a hierarchical surface-code decoder inspired by the renormalization group: a shared local graph neural network processes 3x3x2 space-time syndrome clusters, convolutional layers coarse-grain them, and a GRU integrates over time.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hierarchical reuse is a design pattern that could make neural decoders scale without model bloat.

insights.claim: Because larger code distances add only small convolutional layers, the decoder's parameter count stays bounded at roughly two to three million across distances d = 3, 5, 7 and 9, and it remains trainable on a single commercial GPU.

insights.so_what: Decoder training cost decouples from code distance, lowering the compute barrier for QEC software teams.

themes.theme: Benchmarks on IBM and Google hardware data

insights.claim: On IBM's ibm_berlin (Nighthawk r1) planar memory data, the modular decoder halved logical error per round versus MWPM at d = 3 (1.26% vs 2.60%) and beat it at d = 5 (2.48% vs 3.79%).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Neural decoding offers a large effective error-rate gain on current IBM hardware without hardware changes.

insights.claim: On Google Quantum AI's public below-threshold Sycamore dataset, the decoder reached logical error rates of about 0.638% (d=3), 0.330% (d=5) and 0.179% (d=7), a suppression factor of about 1.9, closely matching AlphaQubit on Z-basis trials.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A single-GPU academic model approximately matches Google DeepMind-class decoding accuracy.

insights.claim: A single neural model fine-tuned across 17 distinct noise settings in an X-type stability sweep on IBM hardware beat per-setting calibrated MWPM at all error rates without retraining.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Robustness to drifting noise reduces recalibration overhead in production QEC.

insights.claim: On a real two-patch d = 3 lattice-surgery ZZ-merge on IBM hardware, the decoder achieved 58.2% joint-parity correlation accuracy versus 56.2% for hardware MWPM and 54.2% uncorrected.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: First evidence neural decoders extend from memory to logic operations, though absolute accuracy remains low.

insights.claim: Prior neural decoders were limited to static memory experiments; this decoder handled multi-patch boundaries by tiling three overlapping GNN encoders across two logical patches and the measurement bridge between them.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Logic-capable decoding is a prerequisite for fault-tolerant algorithms, not just memory demos.

insights.so_what: Decoder latency, not accuracy, is the gating item for neural decoders in fault-tolerant systems.
